[Question] Equipment you bring with you on rides.

Just a quick rant about CO2. Carrying CO2 is not necessary unless you're concerned about the speed of replacing tubes. You're better off with a mini pump or a frame pump. You can use a pump endlessly, but when your cartridges run out because you made a mistake or just got unlucky with too many punctures, you're stranded with no way to get air in the tire. "But tubes can run out too!", you might say. Not really. You can almost always patch a tube on the road if you have no more spares. What you can't do is create more CO2 cartridges out of thin air. CARRY A PUMP. CO2 also seeps out of the tube faster, so you're going to have to refill your tube with a normal pump eventually anyway.

End rant.

Concerning valve converters: if you have a mini pump, it will most likely have its own converter built in. You just unscrew the cap, take out the little piece of rubber, take out the little plastic thing under it, flip that over and put it into the other side of the rubber piece, and screw the whole thing back together. That's how you switch your mini pump between presta and schrader without a special adapter.

My summer kit usually includes: (1) spare tube, (2) tire levers, (1) patch kit, (1) multitool (this guy), (2) energy gels—emergency bonk relief, and (1) mini pump.

I only carry a single spare tube with me, mostly because I don't flat much, but I also generally trust my ability to use a patch kit. If I were running lighter tires, I might consider carrying a 2nd tube. For me, the pump vs. CO2 debate comes down mostly to cost. I don't care about filling a tube fast, and in the long run, the pump will be cheaper than continuing to buy refill cartridges.

One thing I don't see in your inventory is an "emergency" source of calories. I carry a couple of extra gels with me (in addition to any food and water I'd already be carrying for a ride), and they've saved me a few times.

I carry a ten-size wishbone multitool wrench. It won't work for REALLY hard turning (e.g., don't try and lock something down), but it works for most stuff. http://www.ebay.com/itm/New-Bicycle-10-In-1-Dog-Bone-Design-Bike-Mini-Pocket-Hexagon-Wrench-Multi-Tool-/381273069304?hash=item58c5a556f8

Having that wrench saves a lot on weight. I also pack one 5 and 6mm hex wrench- a whole packet is too much weight and space, but just two hex keys isn't much at all. I bring a spare tube (no tire levers needed, huzzah easy-to-change hybrid tires!) though it depends on the ride for whether or not I bring a CO2 kit- they're useful if I'm out in the wilderness or somewhere very remote, but it's often easier to just walk my bike a half mile to the nearest gas service station, car service station, dealership, motorcycle shop, bike shop, or whatever else there is, assuming someone else doesn't stop and offer to help, first. Plus I very rarely get a flat, so I'm contemplating just ditching the tube entirely since I have AAA, which offers me (as a bicyclist) a tow. I recommend AAA if you're also a driver, because that long-distance towing is fucking amazing.

I also carry my swiss army knife with me everywhere (includes screwdriver), and a Spoke Wrench

Overall, this all fits in a camelbak pretty snugly.

Alternatively, if weight isn't much of a concern, I really do recommend the travel kit that Spin Doctor made. I'm not a fan of Performance Bike, but the little ratchet hasn't failed me yet, and it has all the attachments you'll need for your bike, and it gets the job done well enough. Everything fits neatly into the little box, and it is functional.
